name: What is the difference between a T-molding and a reducer strip?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a T-molding and a reducer strip?

acceptedAnswer.text: A T-molding is designed to connect two hard surface floors of the exact same height, creating a flush and seamless look. Its 'T' shape covers the expansion gap between the two floors. In contrast, a reducer strip, also known as a 'threshold reducer' or 'overlap reducer,' is used when one floor is higher than the other. It features a sloped profile that gently transitions from the higher floor down to the lower one, reducing a tripping hazard. Choosing between these depends entirely on the height difference between the two flooring materials you are joining.
acceptedAnswer.description: T-moldings connect floors of the same height, while reducer strips transition from a higher floor to a lower one.
